newsitem.title: UK: UK unveils plan for disarming N Irish guerrillas.
newsitem.headline: UK unveils plan for disarming N Irish guerrillas.

text.p: In a new initiative to breathe life into the Northern Ireland peace process, Prime Minister Tony Blair on Wednesday unveiled to parliament an Anglo-Irish formula for disarming guerrillas in the British-ruled province.

Blair proposed establishing an independent commission to oversee disarmament in parallel with talks on a lasting political settlement, which he said he wanted to start in earnest by early September at the latest and conclude by May.
"I appeal to all the parties to look at the proposals in a constructive spirit. I really do not believe there is another way forward," Blair said.

He said that he was determined to make political progress rapidly and that preparations for substantive multi-party talks would quicken with or without Sinn Fein, the political wing of the outlawed Irish Republican Army.

Blair repeated that an unequivocal restoration of the ceasefire that the IRA broke in February 1996 was needed to win a seat at the talks table for Sinn Fein, which has hitherto insisted that arms should not be handed in until a final political settlement is reached.

"The settlement train is leaving, with or without Sinn Fein. If they want to join, it is absolutely clear what they have to do. I have dealt straight with them. I expect straight dealing in return. We and the other parties will not be waiting around for them," Blair said.
